issue_context.title: August Lock Unprocessable entity error
issue_context.body:
**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
0.98.5

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
a few versions ago, I am not sure

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**
Using the official docker image

**Component/platform:**
https://www.home-assistant.io/components/august/


**Description of problem:**
I can add the entity and it accepts my verification code but when I try to lock/unlock the entity I receive the following:
Failed to call service lock/lock. 422 Client Error: Unprocessable Entity for url: https://api-production.august.com/remoteoperate/{KEYHERE}/lock

**Additional information:**
This was working about a month ago, I am not sure which version it broke on, I have tried completely deleting the entity and integration and re adding it (including the cached config file) and it still persists.

Uggh. I can't believe I didn't think about the bridge. I typically only lock/unlock when I'm close by the unit so the app/HomeKit must be working through Bluetooth. I'm remote right now and just tried the August app and it doesn't work either. When I get home tonight I'll powercycle the bridge but I bet that's it. Will report back.
Confirmed that after power cycling the bridge, everything works. Apologies for the noise.

Unplugging a bridge should be good enough to replicate this.

Better error reporting would likely have avoided this case.  We could probably throw a better exception when we get a 4XX error with JSON in the body.

Note to self: see components/hue/errors.py has an example

Seems like is can also return 423

```
2020-02-12 22:29:38 DEBUG (SyncWorker_15) [august.api] Received API response: 423, b'{"code":97,"message":"Bridge in use"}'
```
Does it make sense to just propagate the “message” up to the the main error?

> Does it make sense to just propagate the “message” up to the the main error?

Unfortunately not all the messages appear to be very consumable so trapping the known ones and giving a useful error is likely going to be the route for this.
